payload.title: Executed analysis (supervisor-reported done): Preregistered nonlinear-sweep analysis

assumptions: Models: Schnakenberg (`f = a − u + u²v`, `g = b − u²v`) and Brusselator (`f = A − (B+1)u + u²v`, `g = Bu − u²v`); 1-D interval, zero-flux (Neumann) ends, γ = 1 (γ only rescales time and length), Du = 1, Dv = ρ·d_c.

Parameter prior (a STATED PRIOR, not published ranges): Schnakenberg `a ~ logU[0.05, 0.4]`, `b ~ logU[0.4, 1.6]`; Brusselator `A ~ U[0.8, 2.5]`, `B = 1 + u·A²` with `u ~ U[0.15, 0.85]`; parameters rounded to small rationals (denominators ≤ 100 / 20). Rejection: well-mixed stable, finite onset ratio `1 < d_c < 400`. Textbook centres exist (Schnakenberg a = 0.1, b = 0.9, d = 10; example source arXiv 1903.05030, seen at search-snippet level only) and lie inside the prior, but the prior is mine. 10 draws per model, drawn with `random.Random(20261031)`.

Distance from onset: `ρ = Dv/d_c ∈ {0.7, 0.9, 0.97, 1.03, 1.1, 1.5, 3.0}`, where `d_c` is the smallest Dv/Du satisfying the `turing-ddi` continuum inequality (computed in floats; Dv = ρ·d_c rounded to denominator ≤ 1000, exact thereafter).

Domain: `L = x·λ_c`, `x ∈ {2, 4, 8}`. Basis: `λ_c = 2π/k_c` with the `turing-wavelength` record notation `k_c² = sqrt(det J/(Du Dv))` evaluated at the onset ratio Dv = d_c (so λ_c does not move with ρ). Basis is a modelling convention, not a cited "realistic" length; `r = L/π` rounded to denominator ≤ 50.

Initial perturbation: band-limited cosine series `Σ_{k=1..K} c_k cos(kπx/L)` (K = max(8, min(N_A/4, 40))) with N(0,1) coefficients scaled so the ANALYTIC std equals `ε·|steady state|` for each species, `ε ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 0.3}`. The same continuous function is sampled by both solvers. Paired seeds `{101, 102}` index the coefficient draw; pairing is across ε, ρ, x and solvers. Design factors are crossed, not iid.
Total grid: 2 models × 10 draws × 7 ρ × 3 x × 3 ε × 2 seeds = **2,520 cells**.
payload.context: Applicability / scope evidence for Delphi claim turing-ddi from a named ensemble of two kinetics models (1-D, zero-flux). Quantities (PREREG definitions, verbatim): R1 = (linear `out_of_scope` ∧ nonlinear `pattern`) / (linear `out_of_scope` cells). Finite-amplitude outcome of the declared model; NOT proof of subcriticality. | R2 = (linear `applies` ∧ nonlinear `no_pattern`) / (linear `applies` cells). "Unstable but no pattern by horizon". Results (REPORT, verbatim): | R1: linear stable, nonlinear patterned | 30 / 1,080 | 2.8% | 1.9–3.9% | | | R2: linear unstable, nonlinear NO pattern by horizon | 0 / 1,440 | 0% | 0–0.26% | This is a sweep over the producer's own ensemble, not a statement about tissue. Declared relation 'qualifies': it qualifies the scope of the claim's linear criterion in this ensemble: cells the criterion calls stable can pattern at finite amplitude (R1), while every linearly unstable cell patterned by the horizon (R2) (a declaration by the importing adapter, not a review and not the producer's own label).
limitations: OpenResearch does not record the execution environment (interpreter, OS, packages, hardware); local runs use the host's own environment and container images are mutable tags, so the record alone does not say how to reproduce the environment.

Run, experiment and project ids are random UUIDs local to one machine's store: there is no shared registry, and the run can be deleted by its owner (`orx exp delete`).
A run reaching status 'done' means the process exited 0. It says nothing about scientific validity and has not been reviewed.
The database exit_code was NULL for this local run; the exit code was read from the run directory's exit_code file instead.

This run read its inputs from, and wrote its outputs to, a directory OUTSIDE the OpenResearch snapshot and run directory. OpenResearch stores neither: the input and output digests here were computed by the adapter from immutable git blobs, and the run itself only links to them through hashes its own script printed.

OpenResearch does not list a run's inputs. Replaying with one of two input files missing produced a different report without any error (measured during this import), so a replayer cannot learn the full input set from the record.

The ensemble is mine (stated prior, three amplitudes, γ = 1, one family of initial perturbations, 1-D Neumann only). A different prior or perturbation family could give different rates; this is a sweep, not a claim about "realistic" parameters.
Both solvers share equations. Solver disagreement (2.3%) is kept as unresolved mass, so the headline rates are bounded rates among all cells rather than among resolved ones.

The analysis script was written after the sweep started (not after seeing results, with one exception: a smoke test of the analyzer on 14 partial rows printed provisional predictions; no design choice was changed afterwards). The PREREG text says "about 08:40"; the commit was made at 08:34 by `date`.

The plain textbook formula (C0) is what predicts "pattern whenever the continuum band exists" regardless of domain; this sweep does not rank it against the gate, it asks about linear-theory limits only.
No GPU or Nebius resources were used. The orx run logged only the analysis, locally.
The orx run covers only the analysis step; the sweep itself ran outside OpenResearch under systemd-run and is not recorded there.
Replay reproduces the analysis from the recorded report inputs; it does not re-run or independently check the 2,520-cell sweep (a separate GPU/CPU replay by the producer is planned, not done).
